newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mayor during Mexican disaster seeks another term.
newsitem.headline: Mayor during Mexican disaster seeks another term.

text.p: The former mayor of Mexico's second largest city, forced out of office after a sewer pipe explosion killed over 200 people in 1992, will try to regain the post in November elections, his party said.

The ruling Institutional Revolution Party (PRI) said on Monday it nominated Enrique Dau Flores, who resigned in disgrace after the disaster but was later acquitted of criminal charges, to seek a new term as mayor of Guadalajara.
Dau will try to recapture the seat from the opposition National Action Party (PAN) in municipal polls on Nov. 9.
"Dau Flores, because of his personal conduct, because of his public conduct, is a guarantee (of success) for our party as candidate," the PRI said in a statement.

The PAN is heavily favored in one poll to regain control of City Hall in the western city of 2 million people, known as the home of mariachi music and more recently as base of some of Mexico's most ruthless drug gangs.

Dau spent eight months in jail for negligence after more than five miles (8 km) of underground drainage pipes exploded, killing 205 people according to the official toll. Unofficial counts ran much higher.
Officials had been warned that gasoline was being dumped in the sewer system. The local newspaper Siglo 21 published a story that morning about the danger.
After Dau spent eight months in jail, a judge dismissed all charges.

The PAN's Cesar Coll Carabias became the first opposition mayor in Guadalajara since the PRI came to power nationally in 1929. The PAN has nominated lawyer Francisco Ramirez Acuna to carry the party flag in the elections.
